headline: THE FED MEETS JULY 29: GOLD SAYS HOLD ALREADY PRICED IN — SILVER HAS THE ASYMMETRIC UPSIDE INTO FOMC WEEK
snippet: GoldSilver.com's FOMC countdown analysis published July 25–26 argues that gold at $4,066 has already priced in the Fed holding rates on July 29 — the 37.9% hike probability embedded in CME FedWatch is the residual uncertainty premium, not the base case. The structural argument: COT speculative net longs trimmed to 183.9K contracts (six-week low) indicates positioning is defensively lean rather than capitulation-flushed, meaning a hold doesn't release pent-up buying so much as confirm what specs already believe. Silver is the asymmetric trade into the binary: at 70:1 ratio against gold and running its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces, a hold removes the only near-term macro headwind against silver's industrial demand premium. The article notes that silver's dual identity — inflation hedge and industrial metal — means it captures upside on a hold (inflation fears subside, industrial outlook improves) while gold consolidates. Target: 67:1 ratio normalization within 30 days of a hold decision would imply $60.60/oz silver at unchanged $4,066 gold. A hike extends compression from a historically depressed base where physical buyers have demonstrably stepped in at $56–58.

headline: SILVER INSTITUTE: GOLD-SILVER RATIO MEAN-REVERTS TO 60:1 — AT 70:1 NOW, SILVER IS STATISTICALLY UNDERVALUED; SIXTH DEFICIT YEAR UNCHANGED AT 46.3M OZ
snippet: The Silver Institute published a GlobeNewswire release July 22 titled 'Gold:Silver Ratio Continues to be Relevant in the Modern Era,' presenting historical analysis showing the ratio has mean-reverted to approximately 60:1 across modern economic cycles. At the current 70:1 ratio, silver is statistically undervalued by 16.7% relative to gold on ratio normalization alone — before any adjustment for silver's sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces, the largest shortfall in the current run. The report distinguishes between short-term ratio widening driven by macro fear (dollar strength, rate-hike pricing) and structural undervaluation driven by supply-demand fundamentals. The Silver Institute's position: the current 70:1 level is anomalous relative to the past decade's 50–65:1 band outside of crisis dislocations (COVID-2020, 2008 peak), and the combination of the deficit structure and ratio deviation creates a compound return setup for silver investors who can tolerate FOMC-event volatility. For junior silver company investors, the ratio argument is an overlay on the equity upside: if silver moves to $67 (60:1 at unchanged gold), silver equity multiples typically expand 2–3x the underlying metal move.

headline: GOLD IS ABOUT TO TRADE 24/7: KALSHI FILES FOR PERPETUAL NO-EXPIRY FUTURES WITH CFTC — CME ALSO LAUNCHED 24/7 GOLD CONTRACTS JULY 26
snippet: GoldSilver.com reported July 25–26 that Kalshi has filed with the CFTC for approval to launch perpetual, no-expiry gold, silver, and platinum futures contracts — instruments with no settlement date that trade continuously, similar to perpetual swap structures common in crypto markets but applied to precious metals for the first time on a regulated U.S. exchange. Simultaneously, CME Group launched its own 24/7 gold trading capability on July 26, 2026, enabling off-hours price discovery during Asian and Middle Eastern sessions when geopolitical and macroeconomic events historically move gold without a liquid U.S. market. The structural implication: 24/7 gold pricing eliminates the gap-open premium that retail traders have historically suffered when holding gold positions over weekends or holidays. For junior mining investors, the market structure development is directionally bullish for gold price stability and discovery — more continuous pricing means geopolitical risk events (Iran, central bank announcements, macro data) get absorbed as they occur rather than creating Monday-open dislocations. The Kalshi application is pending CFTC review; timeline for approval is 90–180 days from filing.

headline: AGNICO EAGLE REPORTS JULY 29: ANALYSTS EXPECT $3.14 EPS (+62%), $3.94B REVENUE — CAMECO FOLLOWS JULY 31 WITH CIGAR LAKE CURTAILMENT UPDATE
snippet: Agnico Eagle Mines (NYSE: AEM) reports Q2 2026 earnings after market close on July 29 — the same day as the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision — with analyst consensus at $3.14 EPS (+62.2% year-over-year) on revenue of $3.94 billion (+40.2% YoY), driven by record gold production across the Canadian Malartic, Detour Lake, and Odyssey underground ramp-up operations. The Barnat Pit production update is expected to confirm full-year guidance at approximately 3.3 million ounces, with investors watching for any revision to the Odyssey underground timeline which would affect long-term reserve life at the world's largest single open-pit gold operation. Cameco Corp (TSX: CCO; NYSE: CCJ) follows on July 31, with the market focused on the Cigar Lake two-week production curtailment in July 2026 and its impact on annual uranium delivery commitments under term contracts. Separately, the Section 232 uranium import review report is expected in late July, with any tariff recommendation potentially a near-term catalyst for domestic U.S. uranium producers including Energy Fuels and Uranium Energy Corp. The July 29 earnings + Fed double-header represents the most event-dense single trading day for senior mining stocks in Q3 2026.

headline: TALAMORE MINING LOCKS IN C$620M COFFEE GOLD CONSTRUCTION PACKAGE — EARLY WORKS UNDERWAY, H1 2027 START; SUPREMO EXTENSION HITS 5.37 g/t OVER 8.4m (TSXV: TALA)
snippet: Talamore Mining Corp. (TSXV: TALA) announced a C$620 million construction financing package for its Coffee Gold Project in Yukon, Canada — one of the largest construction financing packages closed for a junior gold developer at $4,000+ gold. The package includes a C$130 million equity offering that closed July 21, 2026 (bookbuild announced July 7), with early works construction already underway ahead of a formal construction start targeted for H1 2027. Concurrent with the financing news, Talamore released drill results from the Supremo Extension zone: hole CFF-26-152 returned 8.4 metres at 5.37 g/t gold, and hole CFF-26-148 returned 6.6 metres at 6.6 g/t gold — high-grade intercepts that add resource optionality within the existing mine plan footprint. Coffee is one of the few permitted, fully financed gold development projects in the Yukon's White Gold District, a belt that produced multiple major discoveries over the past decade and benefits from existing Yukon infrastructure and a development-friendly First Nations and regulatory framework. At $4,066 gold, C$620 million in committed construction capital eliminates the single largest risk factor in junior gold development — financing uncertainty — leaving execution risk as the primary remaining discount to NAV.

headline: TOCVAN DISCOVERS HIGH-GRADE SILVER-GOLD AT SURFACE 900m FROM PILOT FACILITY — 581 g/t Ag IN SONORA AS Q4 2026 PRODUCTION APPROACHES (CSE: TOC)
source_name: Investing News Network / Tocvan Ventures Corp.
snippet: Tocvan Ventures Corp. (CSE: TOC) announced July 23, 2026 the discovery of a new high-grade silver-gold zone at surface approximately 900 metres east of the Pilot Facility at its Gran Pilar Project in Sonora, Mexico. Drill hole JES-26-152 returned 1.5 metres at 2.2 g/t gold and 581 g/t silver — a bonanza-grade silver intercept that confirms a new vein structure outside the established resource. Four holes collectively confirm a robust vein system with multiple high-grade silver-gold intervals at surface depths, the kind of geometry that supports underground selective mining at high margins. Tocvan is approaching the Q4 2026 doré production milestone at its Pilot Facility, making the new zone discovery simultaneously a near-term exploration catalyst and a potential production expansion opportunity. For junior silver investors, the 581 g/t silver intercept in Sonora — Mexico's most productive silver state — at a project within 900 metres of existing processing infrastructure is a rare combination: high-grade discovery cost is minimal because metallurgical infrastructure is already built, meaning new resources convert to production economics faster than a greenfield discovery in the same geology.

headline: TORR METALS CONFIRMS DEEP COPPER-GOLD PORPHYRY AT 400m+ DEPTH AT BERTHA NORTH, KOLOS BC — PHASE II ADVANCES MULTI-STAGE VEINING AND CHALCOPYRITE MODEL (TSXV: TMET)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Torr Metals Inc.
snippet: Torr Metals Inc. (TSXV: TMET) reported July 22, 2026 Phase II drill results from the Bertha North target at its 332 km² Kolos Project in BC's prolific Toodoggone district, confirming a deep copper-gold porphyry system at 400 metres-plus depth. The intercepts show extensive hydrothermal brecciation, multi-stage copper-gold veining, and chalcopyrite + chalcocite sulphide mineralization persisting to approximately 580 metres vertical — the depth profile consistent with a high-temperature porphyry core rather than a near-surface oxide cap. Hematitic potassic alteration is present throughout, the textbook signature of a well-preserved, fertile copper porphyry that has not been oxidized or leached. The Toodoggone district hosts the past-producing Kemess copper-gold mine and several development-stage porphyry systems that have attracted senior producer interest at $6.30/lb copper. For copper development investors, Bertha North's Phase II confirmation that the system extends beyond 400 metres depth is critical: porphyry copper deposits must demonstrate vertical continuity to support the multi-decade mine lives that large-scale open-pit economics require, and the 180-metre mineralization envelope confirmed in Phase II passes that test.

headline: QMINES KICKS OFF 10,000m DRILL AT MT CHALMERS — 18m AT 2.7 g/t Au AND 1.7% Cu IN FIRST HOLE; THREE RIGS RUNNING IN QUEENSLAND (ASX: QML)
snippet: QMines Ltd. (ASX: QML) commenced its largest-ever drill program at the Mt Chalmers Copper-Gold Project near Rockhampton, Queensland, with 10,000 metres planned across three simultaneously operating rigs — and the first intercept, MCDD003, returned 18 metres at 2.7 g/t gold and 1.7% copper from 127 metres depth, including a 12-metre zone at 3.8 g/t gold and 2.0% copper. The program has two concurrent objectives: definitive feasibility study support drilling to increase confidence in the known resource, and step-out drilling to extend the resource envelope in directions indicated by the structural model. Mt Chalmers is a VMS-style copper-gold system in Queensland's productive Bowen Basin, a jurisdiction with established mining infrastructure and an operating copper circuit at the nearby Ernest Henry Mine that represents a potential processing pathway. At $6.30/lb copper and $4,066 gold, the 18-metre intercept at combined precious and base metal grades puts Mt Chalmers in the top quartile of Australian copper-gold drill results year-to-date. The 10,000-metre scope — three times the company's previous largest campaign — signals management confidence in the resource scale and DFS timeline.

headline: LITHIUM CRASHES TO 5-MONTH LOW ON RESTART FEARS THEN REBOUNDS — THREE FACTORS CAP BATTERY METALS UPSIDE AS COBALT AND NICKEL FLOOR HOLDS
snippet: A NAI500 July 2026 market analysis documents lithium carbonate prices crashing to 136,800 yuan per tonne on July 22 — a five-month low driven by restart fears as mothballed Australian and South American operations signal potential return to production — before recovering to 144,000 yuan/t. Three structural factors capping further upside even at recovery prices: (1) restarted lithium supply from high-cost operations threatening a 2027 glut if EV demand growth decelerates below 25%; (2) EV demand fragility in key markets (Europe and North America) contrasting with stationary energy storage demand surging 51% year-over-year, which consumes different battery chemistry profiles; (3) price destruction at Chinese industrial breakeven levels where downstream cathode manufacturers cannot pass costs through. Floors are provided by the Democratic Republic of Congo cobalt export ban (restricting cobalt supply to Chinese battery manufacturers) and Indonesia's nickel production quotas for 2026. For battery metals junior investors, the analysis distinguishes the current period from 2021-2022's speculative run: the demand is real but the supply response is faster and more elastic than anticipated, suggesting sustained prices require demand growth acceleration rather than supply constraint alone.

headline: 3 URANIUM STOCKS TO BUY BEFORE JULY ENDS — SECTION 232 REPORT DUE, CAMECO Q2 ARRIVES JULY 31; URANIUM HOLDS $86/LB UP 20% YEAR-OVER-YEAR
snippet: 24/7 Wall St. published July 23 a uranium sector catalyst roundup identifying three stocks ahead of two near-term binary events: the Section 232 uranium import review report (expected late July 2026) and Cameco's Q2 earnings release on July 31. The three: Cameco Corp (NYSE: CCJ) — the world's largest publicly traded uranium producer with 18 million pounds of annual production and Cigar Lake disruption transparency expected in Q2 disclosure; Uranium Energy Corp (NYSE: UEC) — the most U.S.-leveraged pure-play uranium miner with Wyoming ISR operations directly exposed to any Section 232 import tariff outcome; and Centrus Energy Corp (NYSE: LEU) — the only U.S. company licensed to enrich uranium with domestic enrichment capacity, which crushed Q1 2026 EPS estimates by 289% on a $3.8 billion contract backlog running through 2040. Uranium spot held at approximately $86/lb — up 20% year-over-year — as demand from 31 new reactor builds globally and U.S. nuclear capacity reinstatement legislation continues to absorb available supply. The Section 232 report, if recommending import tariffs or quota restrictions, would be the most significant domestic uranium policy action since the 1990s.

headline: GOLD FELL 20% FROM ITS ATH BUT THE BULL CASE IS INTACT — FED SPLIT 9-8 ON PAUSES, CPI COOLED TO 3.5%, CENTRAL BANKS BOUGHT 244t IN Q1 2026
snippet: GoldSilver.com's July 2026 gold price outlook addresses the 20% correction from gold's all-time high to $4,063 and argues the structural bull case is unchanged across four pillars. First, the Federal Reserve's rate pause decision was reportedly passed 9-8 — an unusually narrow margin that reveals deep internal disagreement about whether inflation is sufficiently controlled to justify unchanged rates, suggesting rate cut probability is higher than the 37.9% hike odds currently priced imply for the second half of 2026. Second, June CPI printed 3.5% — down from 4.2% in March — confirming the disinflation trajectory despite the Iran-oil spike, removing the most bearish scenario where inflation re-accelerates and forces an emergency rate hike. Third, central banks globally purchased 244 tonnes of gold in Q1 2026, the highest quarterly total since records began — a demand floor that does not exist in any other asset class. Fourth, year-end 2026 gold price targets from five major institutional forecasters range from $4,500 to $6,300, a consensus that reflects structural dollar debasement expectations rather than momentum extrapolation. The article concludes that $4,063 represents a technically healthy correction after the $5,075 ATH, not a trend reversal, and that the current price is the entry point the prior ATH made impossible.
